entries: You gain three close contacts which you can call upon to aid you on your adventures. These contacts are Humanoids that use the Contact stat block shown below. You determine their appearance. Over the course of an hour, which can take place during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can summon one of these contacts to your side. Your contact acts independently of you, but it obeys your commands.

The contact acts during your turn. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command it to take an action in its stat block or another action. If you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, the contact acts on its own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.
entries.name: Combat

entries: A contact dies if it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or is dismissed when you die. You can replace a dead contact over the course of 24 hours and by spending 100 GP.
entries.name: Disappearance of your Contact

entries: You can't have more than one contact active at a time. If you summon another contact while one is active, the previous one is dismissed.
entries.name: One Contact Only

feat.name: Friends in Low Places

entries: You are a member of the upper class, and it shows. You gain the following benefits.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} of Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks when interacting with members of the upper class.
entries.name: Mark of Nobility

entries: You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to snap an ally back into focus. Choose one ally that can hear you within 120 feet of you that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB}. That condition ends on the ally and they gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
entries.name: Noble Presence

feat.name: Noble Bearing

entries: You gain the following benefits.

When an ally you can see within 30 feet of you would be hit by an attack and take damage, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to intercept the attack. You move to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of that ally, and all effects of the attack are moved onto you. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
If you are dropped to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} after using this feature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Death Saving Throws until you are {@variantrule Stable|XPHB}, or die.
entries.name: Interception

entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks to convince people to let you help them.
entries.name: Righteous Protector

feat.name: Protector

entries: Through some means you have developed glands that allow you to spit acid, gaining the following benefits.
You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid damage.
entries.name: Acid Resistance

entries: You have acid glands which count as a simple ranged weapon you are proficient with, and can be used when making Unarmed Strikes. Your acid spit has a range of 30 / 90 and {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}, and deals {@dice 1d6} {@item Acid|XPHB} damage on a hit.
entries.name: Spit

feat.name: Acid Glands

entries: You gain the following benefits.
You can breathe both air and water.
entries.name: Amphibious

entries: You gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
entries.name: Swim Speed

feat.name: Amphibious

entries: A connection with The Artist enhances your tricky mind to find clever new spins on old techniques. You gain the following benefits.
You learn two cantrips of your choice from any spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).
entries.name: Two Cantrips

entries: You learn the {@spell Fabricate|XPHB} spell, and can cast it without expending a spell slot. When you cast it in this way, it has a casting time of an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} and a duration of 10 minutes. After casting it in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level, but with the normal casting time and duration.
entries.name: Fabricate

feat.name: Artist's Creative Conjuring

entries: Your exposure to House Varley’s blood magic has changed you, granting you the following benefits:

Choose one level 1 spell from the {@filter Evocation or Transmutation|spells|level=1|school=V;T} school of magic. You always have that spell and the {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either spell in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.
entries.name: Blood Magic

feat.name: Blood-Touched

entries: You gain the following benefits.

Choose one creature you have indefinitely summoned by a class feature, Feat, or the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} or {@spell Find Steed|XPHB} spells. That creature gains one of the following Feats of your choice: {@feat Athlete|XPHB}, {@feat Charger|XPHB}, {@feat Heavy Armor Master|XPHB}, {@feat Medium Armor Master|XPHB}, {@feat Martial Adept|XPHB}, or {@feat Speedy|XPHB}.
These benefits persist even after the creature is dismissed, resummoned, or changes form.
entries.name: Companion Training

feat.name: Companion Trainer

entries: You gain the following benefits.
Choose one creature you have summoned using the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell. Its {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases by 1, to a maximum of 6.

In addition, it gains one of the following Feats of your choice: Blood-Touched, {@feat Fey-Touched|XPHB}, {@feat Grappler|XPHB}, {@feat Lucky|XPHB}, {@feat Mage Slayer|XPHB}, {@feat Magic Initiate|XPHB}, {@feat Martial Adept|XPHB}, {@feat Savage Attacker|XPHB}, {@feat Shadow-Touched|XPHB}, {@feat Skilled|XPHB}, {@feat Skulker|XPHB}, {@feat Tavern Brawler|XPHB}, {@feat Telekinetic|XPHB}, {@feat Telepathic|XPHB}, or {@feat Tough|XPHB}. If the Feat doesn't already provide an ability score increase, you can increase one of your familiar's ability scores by 1, to a maximum of 20.
These benefits persist even after the familiar is dismissed, resummoned, or changes form.
entries.name: Familiar Training

feat.name: Familiar Trainer

entries: A connection with the Lovers gifts you a dual nature. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you create a perfect copy of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of yourself. This feature lasts for 1 minute, but ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. When this feature ends, you decide which version is the real you.

While this copy persists, you are considered to be occupying both spaces at once. Both versions share all game statistics and any effects that are applied to them. It is impossible to discern which is the real you.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. While your Gemini is active, the following rules apply:
entries.name: Gemini

entries: Actions you take that target others can originate from either version of you, you choose when you take that action.
items.name: Actions

entries: When moving, only one version of you moves, but you can divide your movement between your two versions in any way you like.
items.name: Movement

entries: When only one version of you takes damage from any given source, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage. If both versions are subjected to an area effect, such as from the {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell, you make one saving throw and take the effects as normal.
items.name: Shared Suffering

feat.name: Lovers' Duality

entries: A connection with The Paragon has gifted you with power to protect your body and convictions. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you wreath yourself in the energies of the Paragon for 10 minutes. This effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. When you activate this feature and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns, you can grant yourself or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to 3 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. While a creature has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to end or avoid the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, and against spells from the Illusion or Enchantment schools. Any {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} remaining at the end of the duration are lost.
Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}
entries.name: Paragon's Ward

feat.name: Paragon's Ward

entries: You have built a tolerance to poison and weaponized it for your own usage, giving you the following benefits.
You gain resistance to Poison damage and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.
entries.name: Poison Resistance

entries: As an action, you can exhale a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of poisonous gas. All creatures in that area must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d12} Poison damage, or half as much on a successful one.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d12} at levels 5 ({@dice 2d12}), 11 ({@dice 3d12}), and 17 ({@dice 4d12}).
entries.name: Poison Breath

feat.name: Poisonous

entries: Through a natural or alchemical process you have developed a sharp natural weapon, ensuring you are never unarmed, giving you the following benefits.

You grow claws (Slashing), fangs (Piercing), horns (Piercing), or hooves (Bludgeoning). This new growth counts as a simple melee weapon you are proficient with, and can be used when making Unarmed Strikes. The natural weapon has {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}, and deals {@damage 1d6} damage of the type in parentheses on a hit.
entries.name: Natural Weapon

feat.name: Primal Mutation

entries: A connection with The Savant allows you to know your enemy with each strike you take. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you wreath yourself in the energies of the Savant for 1 minute. This effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. For the duration, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you also deal {@damage 1d8} Psychic damage and pull knowledge about that creature. Choose one of the following statistics from below, and the DM reveals that information about the creature to you:

On a critical hit, the target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + the ability score modifier used for the attack roll. On a failure, the DM reveals the entire stat block to you as the Savant's guidance leads to critical, comprehensive information related to your quarry. On a success, you choose two pieces of information from the list above to be revealed by the DM. You can deal this damage and gain this information only once per turn.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
entries.name: Savant's Inquiry

feat.name: Savant's Inquiry

entries: A connection with The Shepherd allows you to lend aid to your allies. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you wreath yourself in the energies of the Shepherd for 1 minute. This effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. When you activate this ability and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns, you can target a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your Constitution modifier or ends one condition on itself from {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, or {@condition Deafened|XPHB}.

This ability can only be called forth during combat. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
entries.name: Shepherd's Embrace

feat.name: Shepherd's Embrace

feat.name: Tool Expert

entries: A connection with The Warden has granted you the pragmatism to make difficult but necessary choices. You gain the following benefits.

You always have the {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast this spell without expending a spell slot, and when you do, the magic of the Warden deepens the bond. When one of the creatures bonded with the spell takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give the creature {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage, and you receive the same amount of damage.

Once you cast this spell in this way, you can't cast it in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this Feat).

feat.name: Warden's Bond

entries.name: Ability Score Increase

entries: When you hit a target with a whip as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target. This damage equals your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
entries.name: Crack

entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature no more than one sizer larger than you with a whip, you can force it to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + the ability score modifier used to make the attack) or suffer one of the following effects:
The creature drops one item it is holding, which falls harmlessly to the ground in its space.
items.name: Disarm

items.name: Grapple

entries: The creature falls {@condition Prone|XPHB}.
items.name: Trip

entries.name: Whip Mastery

feat.name: Whip Master

You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

feat.name: Wings Unfurled

entries: A connection with the Wolf has gifted you with power to press your foes, granting you the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can mark one creature you can see within 30 feet of you and immediately move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} towards it. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

While marked, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls targeting any creature other than you. Additionally, you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} and can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} so long as you are moving towards the marked creature.

This mark lasts for 1 minute, and ends early if you use this ability to mark a different creature, if you end your turn more than 60 feet away from the marked creature, or when you or the marked creature becomes {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Arachne Lineage

entries: Akin to centaurs, these creatures of the Underdark have the upper body of a humanoid, and the lower body of an arachnid. Their humanoid skin is often starkly pale, intermittent with colouration or patterning matching their arachnid body.

Arachne can be found in small roving families hunting the various beasts that make this dangerous subterranean land their home. An arachne is a rare sight outside of these family units, and even more so on the surface; Their monstrous appearance tends to draw fear or disgust, though they are known to trade with drow enclaves, who see them in a similar light to driders.

When food is scarce, the strongest among their family will leave to forge their own path, allowing the family a better chance at surviving the shortages. These lone arachne may join a different family in their journey or become fully independent.
Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)

entries: To the people at large, the Burrowfolk have the most difficulty with life in Altoras. Forced to choose between living in the underground city of New Burrow ruled by the mob or on the Kaiju-infested jungles of Muhana above, they are often drawn to seedy tactics and underhanded methods just to get by. Their cunning, curiosity, and strong survival instincts make them perfect for the job.

Though this is the unfortunate situation for most Burrowfolk, they are no more naturally violent or larcenous than others. But old stereotypes linger, especially with the affluent of New Burrow actively putting their interests above all else.
Burrowfolk are short humanoids that closely resemble members of the rodent family. They mature quickly, often reaching adulthood by age 12, but still live about as long as Humans.

entries: Once part of the Kamarilik expedition to Jagara, gilblin were once ordinary goblins. When the colony was forced into the sea, the adaptive nature of the goblins allowed them to take on qualities that facilitated their survival. Now they work with the koalinth in their underwater city, trying to carve a home for themselves beneath the waves.

Much like their land-dwelling ancestors, gilblin are short goblinoids with long pointed ears, broad noses, and a penchant for mischief. But their similarities are as numerous as their differences; gilblin skin and hair comes most often in deep blues and greens, but red is also known to appear. They have fins extending from their forearms, complete with webbed hands and feet.

Their most interesting feature is their water jet, an organ found in their hands or throat that propels an intense stream of water. In the sea, it is a purely defensive mechanism, a surprise show of force to unwanted guests. Above water, however, it allows the gilblin to hunt flying prey, disorienting the unsuspecting creature and bringing it closer to where the gilblin can pounce.

You can deal this damage a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
entries.name: Quills

entries: The Kor'Rokka of the Koh'Harrun League have resided on the Harra Archipelago for hundreds of years. While the League is a collection of island nations that are populated mostly by Humans, Tritons, and Sea Elves, the Kor'Rokka have integrated into the League and can be found throughout the different cities that dot the islands.

Kor'Rokka have impressive regenerative powers, capable of preventing their bodies from aging. It's because of this that scholars believe the Kor'Rokka are related to trolls, but question whether this ancestry occurs naturally. While they may be physically intimidating, the Kor'Rokka are a generally reserved people, with a culture that values inner peace and careful consideration of one's actions.

Kor'Rokka are reminiscent of trolls in their towering, slender builds and prominent underbite, but that's mostly where the comparison ends. They are an amphibious species complete with webbed fingers and toes, colorful patterning, and sharp quills adorning various parts of their body. When a Kor' Rokka has come of age they choose a name they feel represents them, this name is often a deed, a natural force or entity that they want to embody, or a virtue. This name is private and only given to those closest to them.

entries: The Gnolls of Altoras are hyena-like humanoids known for their savage martial prowess and distinctive cackle. Commonly found in the forests and plains of Cennverai, these people roam the land in clans, the Matriarch being both the most powerful warrior and the wisest leader. These clans are mostly self-sustaining through living off the land or raiding nearby trade caravans.

Their clan activities often lead to them avoiding civilization and being rejected in kind, but beyond the spurn for battle and the menacing laugh are a people capable of the strongest kinship. Those that leave their clans are almost never seen in solitary; Gnolls are powerful and staunch allies, always willing to put their life on the line for their chosen family.

entries: The Grung are brightly coloured frog-like humanoids that were originally subjects of the Yuan-ti, at the bottom of the social ladder. They are skilled hunters and assassins, using ambush tactics and their natural poisons to subdue enemies. The tough pads on their fingers and toes allow them to cling to nearly any surface, and stalk the jungle canopies away from danger and on the prowl.

Using their unique skill sets, they were eventually able to rebel against the Yuan-ti and create their own foothold in the jungles of Muhana and Jagara, forming tribes and their own caste system based on skin color.
Small (about 2-4 feet tall)

entries: As an action, you begin to sing a luring song. Choose a number of creatures up to or equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} within 60 feet of you that can hear you. Those creatures must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier) or be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you until the end of your next turn. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, if the target is more than 5 feet from you, the target must move on its turn towards you by the most direct route, trying to get within 5 feet of you. It doesn't avoid {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}; however, before moving into damaging terrain (such as lava or a pit) and whenever it takes damage, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on a success.

On subsequent turns, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to extend the duration of your song to the end of your next turn, up to a maximum of 1 minute. Your song ends early if you choose to end it (no action required), become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or die.
After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.
entries.name: Luring Song

entries: Harpies are the people of legend amongst sailors of the Root Sea League. Sometimes called sirens, they have mostly humanoid bodies, but with scaly legs, clawed feet and hands, and feathers adorning their body akin to scavenging birds, including their large wings. By other humanoid standards, all harpies are female-presenting, which has led some to believe male harpies don't exist. This rumour is unfounded; the reality is that harpies are all intersex, and simply appear "female". The flock acts as one family unit, each member taking turns scavenging and child rearing. Gendered language and roles are virtually nonexistent.

Harpies use their cunning and magical gift of song to lure sailors into harm's way, scavenging on their remains. Every harpy sings a distinct song. While some songs are said to be heartbreaking in their beauty, others are wretched squawking and compel only the magically enthralled.

This cultural practice has garnered a contentious relationship amidst other island nations as well as between harpy flocks. Some flocks have abandoned this tradition, exclusively engaging in scavenging rather than actively leading others to danger, while others still have begun to hunt fish and crustaceans.

entries: Residing deep in the deserts of the Planes of Ruin, the jackalwere live in large packs alongside lamia. It is said they were born as servants to a great demon, transformed from ordinary jackals into shape-shifting tricksters. Jackalweres are easily mistaken for werewolves in this respect, but jackalweres aren't supernaturally afflicted -- their jackal forms are their natural state.

Their shapeshifting powers, abyssal heritage, and deceitful nature have garnered them a frightful reputation among the bandits scattered through the Planes -- a reputation that is not entirely unearned, as the jackalwere are known to be fiendishly capable of luring those crossing through their territory into ambushes. For the eldest of the species, it's said the simple act of telling the truth was physically painful, though this trait is not necessarily carried by modern jackalweres.

entries: The Requiem are a displaced group of divine humanoids, survivors from a universe before this one that was completely unmade. The Requiem are innately tied to the Song of Creation, so while all felt the despair of the end of the Universe from facing their mortality, The Requiem also felt it innately, deeply connected to the very thing being unraveled. When their world was destroyed a small population fled aboard the Mythallar, a magic stasis pod that could sustain them outside of the Universe for millennia. Now, having woken from the Mythallar in a brand new world that's reminiscent of their lost one, they are trying to make Altoras a new home for the future generations born here connected to this reality.

Created by a long-dead god that preceded The Seven in the image of his lost daughter, most Requiem are born female-presenting with tall and slender features reminiscent of Elves. They mature at the same rate as Humans, but live slightly longer - up to 150 years - thanks to the divine resilience granted by their creator.

While they're usually found in the Feywild, satyrs do wander to other planes of existence, most often to the Material Plane. Despite their formidable build, bugbears - known as Tak'Garun in their homeland of Arovatan - are a serene and disciplined people, grounded in the relentless pursuit of personal and communal excellence. Central to Tak'Garun philosophy is a steadfast commitment to tranquility and unwavering focus.

entries: Alongside the lizardfolk and medusa, the yuan-ti of Altoras have dominated the jungles of Muhana and Jagara for untold centuries. In ancient times, they were once human, and were blessed by the great leviathan the Storm Serpent to survive the harsh jungles. This blessing transformed them, creating the yuan-ti.

Yuan-ti appear mostly human but with notable serpentine features such as slitted eyes, scaly skin, and forked tongues. Scale colors are usually simple greens and browns, but more elaborate swirls, stripes, or diamond patterns are possible, even in blues and reds.

Yuan-ti society is structured into a strict religious caste system -- The more snake features you have, the closer you are to the image of the Storm Serpent, the more responsibility to have to the temples, and thus the more respect you are owed. These leaders of the people undergo sacred rituals to morph their bodies even further, transforming themselves into malisons with higher power, or abominations ever higher.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with your tendrils, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier) or be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.
items.name: Mutation (Stinging Tendrils)

entries: As a koalinth, you have these special traits.
You can breathe both air and water. You also have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
entries.name: Amphibious

entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can release a burst of water from valves in your skin, teleporting yourself to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.
entries.name: Aquatic Surge

entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.
entries.name: Darkvision

entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition
entries.name: Fey Ancestry

entries: Each koalinth has taken on a mutation to help them adapt to their watery environment. Choose one of the following mutations, and you gain its benefits:

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can blend into your environment and gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. This trait lasts until you move, make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.
items.name: Camouflage

entries: Your carapace provides you a base AC of 16 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You can't wear light, medium, or heavy armor, but if you are using a shield, you can apply the shield's bonus as normal.
items.name: Chitinous Carapace

entries: As the Jagara expedition was beginning to fail, the hobgoblins knew they were destined to be pushed into the sea or perish. The arcanists of the expedition, with the help of their goblin compatriots, were able to mix the naturally adaptive goblin essence and qualities of creatures within the sea. The result is the koalinth: slender hobgoblins with bright colouration, gills, and webbed hands and feet.

Much like their ancestors, the koalinth are highly structured and militaristic. With their new adaptations and military prowess, they have since become an established nation on the coasts of Jagara, and are ready to rejoin the world stage.

race.name: Koalinth

entries: As an ogura, you have these special traits.

When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can consume the flesh of a dead creature to gain power and insight. You can ask the DM {@dice 1d4} questions about something the creature has experienced in life, as the memories of those experiences are conferred to you through its flesh. Additionally, you gain one {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and proficiency in one skill that the creature had in life (you choose from the available stat block). If none are available, you gain one that is deemed appropriate by the DM. These bonuses last until you use this trait again.
entries.name: Enlightened Consumption

entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level.
entries.name: Ogre Toughness

entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any saving throw you make to avoid the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.
entries.name: Powerful Build

entries: Deep in the jungles of Jagara, a tribe of humans made an ancient pact with a tribe of ogres. Over time, the two groups would merge into the ogura. Sometimes called half-ogres, the ogura are towering humanoids with intense appetites and a thick build to match. The union between human and ogre has granted the ogura unique magic that allows them to draw strength from the things that they consume. Using this power, they have carved out a nation for themselves in the dense and unyielding jungles.

Their most prominent threat is the yuan-ti, who claim dominion over all of Jagara. In competition to their dinosaur mounts, the ogura have made a culture of taming and utilizing forest drakes to ride in thunderous formations.

race.name: Ogura

entries: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)
sizeEntry.name: Size:

entries: As a lamia, you have these special traits.

When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a corrupting touch, forcing one creature within 5 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d8} Psychic damage. If it fails by 5 or more, it is also {@condition Charmed|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach character levels 5 ({@dice 2d8}), 11 ({@dice 3d8}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8}).
entries.name: Corrupting Touch

entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.
entries.name: Darkvision

entries: You know the *Minor Illusion* cantrip. You also know the *Disguise Self* spell, and you always have this spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this trait's spells (choose when you select this species).
entries.name: Innate Spells

entries: With a 10-foot running start, you can {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} up to 30 feet.
entries.name: Leap

entries: Lamia are centaur-like creatures, their lower body resembling a lion and their upper body that of a humanoid. Though their origins are not well understood, it is said an ambitious ruler made a pact with a great demon for everlasting majesty. They were given a beautiful visage, enchanting magic, and jackalwere servants, but were simultaneously transformed into the monstrous lamia.

In the Planes of Ruin, modern lamia live in tight-knit prides or packs alongside jackalwere. They often dwell near ruins, seeking mysterious magic they can use to gain riches and influence. Lamias use magical illusions and enchantments to trick others into serving them, or luring them into ambushes. Lone lamia can be exiled from the pride or striking out as adventurers in search of their own riches and influence.

race.name: Lamia

sizeEntry.name: Size:

entries: As a marilin, you have these special traits.

You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire and Poison damage. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on yourself.
entries.name: Abyssal Resilience

entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.
entries.name: Darkvision

entries: You have an extra set of arms. These arms can be used to take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, hold shields, weapons, foci, or material components, or make somatic components to cast spells.
entries.name: Extra Arms

entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. Additionally, you can use your snake body to Grapple targets. While a target is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by your body, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your turns to constrict the target, dealing {@damage 2d6} Bludgeoning damage.
entries.name: Serpentine Body

entries: Marilin often get confused for members of yuan-ti enclaves, but their origins lie in the depths of the abyss. While many of the humans who would move to Jagara would turn to the Storm Serpent, the people who would eventually become the marilin chose to call upon a great marilith, and it bestowed them with the gifts that made it such a feared warrior. The humans grew an extra pair of arms and a large constricting snake as a tail.

Thanks to this patronage, the marilin have become a nation of adept hunters and warriors. During sacred rituals, they offer up great beasts to the marilith. Though they remain mostly solitary, the marilin are often in conflict with the yuan-ti for hunting their dinosaurs.

race.name: Marilin

You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.
entries.name: Darkvision

entries.name: Snake Hair

entries: As a Magic action, each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier) or be {@condition Restrained|XPHB}. The target remakes this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success, or becoming {@condition Petrified|XPHB} instead of {@condition Restrained|XPHB} on a second failed save.
After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.
entries.name: Petrifying Gaze

entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace any attack with a poison ray. This ray is a ranged spell attack with a range of 120 feet, and deals Poison damage equal to {@dice 1d10} + your Constitution modifier on a hit. Constitution is your spellcasting ability modifier for your ray.
entries.name: Poison Ray

entries: When the magic that once transformed the yuan-ti mutated, the medusa were born. Unlike their yuan-ti cousins, however, medusae see their powers as a curse.

Though many still live in yuan-ti enclaves, the divide between the two peoples has grown steadily over time. Medusae don't fit in the traditional caste system, and their clear disdain for their "gifts" further expands the rift.

It's not uncommon for medusae to pursue solitary paths, spending time away to control their petrifying powers or carve their own path. Some have even founded monastic traditions deep in the jungles, using meditation and the monastic lifestyle to find inner peace and camaraderie.

Typical medusae have scaly skin of earthy colours, ranging from light browns to deep blacks. Their infamous petrifying gaze is noted in the intense red glow of their eyes and, instead of hair, their heads are covered in a mass of living venomous serpents.

Hit or miss, choose one ally within 30 feet of the target. That ally gains a +1 bonus on the first attack roll they make against the target until the start of your next turn.
The damage increases by +1 when you reach levels 5 (+2), 11 (+3), and 17 (+4).

spell.name: Accompanying Note

entries: You weave a ward of force to protect an ally within range. Until the start of your next turn, the target has a +3 bonus to its AC (including against the triggering attack) and takes no damage from the Magic Missile spell. This spell does not stack with the Shield spell.
spell.name: Blanche's Reactive Warding

entries: When this spell is cast on the gemstone, it records whatever is spoken within the next 10 minutes in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} around the stone. The recording lasts until the duration of the spell has ended, the stone is destroyed, or the spell is cast again on the same stone. The recording can be played back at any point during the duration as an action, and ends early when you choose to (no action required). The play back can be done by anyone holding the stone.
spell.name: Commemorate to Stone

entries: You touch the ground and channel magic through the earth. One creature that you can see within range expends a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} Die, rolls it, and regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the value rolled plus your spellcasting ability modifier.
The number of Hit Point Dice expended increases by 1 at levels 5 (2), 11 (3), and 17 (4).
entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade

spell.name: Earthen Revitalization

entries: The spell sharpens your reflexes, bolsters your fortitude, and strengthens your resolve. Until the start of your next turn, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all saving throws (including against the triggering effect).
spell.name: Heighten Resilience

time.condition: which you take when you fail a saving throw

The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 1.
entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot

spell.name: Infernal Strike

entries: A bead of white energy streaks toward a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage. If the target is not missing any of its hit points, it instead takes {@damage 1d12} Radiant damage.
The damage increases by one die when you reach levels 5 ({@dice 2d8} or {@dice 2d12}), 11 ({@dice 3d8} or {@dice 3d12}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8} or {@dice 4d12}).
entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade

entries: You produce a shard of glass or gemstone and shatter it. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage.
The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} at levels 5 ({@dice 2d6}), 11 ({@dice 3d6}), and 17 ({@dice 4d6}).
entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade

spell.name: Scattershot

entries: As you hit the target, the projectile detonates in a shower of fireflies and powdered snow. The target and each creature within 5 feet of the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage. Until the spell ends, each creature sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 5-foot radius, attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, and it can't benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.
The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each spell slot level above 1.
entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot

spell.name: Snow Flurry Shot

entries: A 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of grass and flowers begins to grow on a point on the ground you can see within range. Creatures of your choice within that area when it appears regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability modifier.

For the duration, when a creature of your choice starts its turn in the area, it regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability modifier. If a creature has already been healed by this spell, it instead gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability modifier. These {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} disappear when the spell ends.
The healing increases by {@dice 2d6} for each spell slot level above 3.
entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot

spell.name: Squemlish's Friend Zone

entries: You run your hands through a willing creature’s hair and change its color, shape, form, and length, up to 1 foot longer or shorter. If you cast the spell multiple times, you can have up to three creatures styled at a time, and you can dismiss its effects as an action.
spell.name: Style Shift

components.m: a grain of sand and a small piece of coal

entries: Choose a point you can see within range. A rapidly expanding star appears in a 5-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point.

Each creature in that area must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@dice 1d8} Radiant, {@dice 1d8} Cold, and {@damage 1d8} Fire damage, or half as much on a success. A creature also makes that save if it enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature makes that save only once per turn.

At the start of each of your turns, the radius of the star expands by 5 feet. When the spell ends, the star explodes in a 20-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}, plus another 5 feet radius for every round you maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@dice 1d8} Radiant, {@dice 1d8} Cold, and {@damage 1d8} Fire damage, plus another {@dice 1d8} of each damage type for every round you maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.
The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 5.
entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot

spell.name: Zahlia's Collapsing Star

entries: Your lower body is that of a scorpion, easily recognized by grasping pincers and a long segmented tail ending with a stinger. You have these additional traits.

Your claws are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deals {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. When you hit a creature with your claws as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can use both the {@variantrule Damage|XPHB} and the {@variantrule Grapple|XPHB} option from {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. You can use this benefit only once per turn.
entries.name: Gripping Claws

entries: Your stinger is a simple melee weapon which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a hit. Once per turn, you can also deal {@damage 2d6} Poison damage when you hit a creature with your stinger.
entries.name: Poison Stinger

subrace.name: Scorpion

entries: Your lower body is that of a spider, with an enlarged thorax and abdomen ending in spinnerets. You have these additional traits.

As an action, you can conjure a mass of webbing at a point within 60 feet of you. The webs fill a 20-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} there for 1 hour. The webs are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and the area within them is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}.

The first time a creature enters the webs on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier) or have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition while in the webs or until it takes an action to free itself.

The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} of webs exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing {@damage 2d4} Fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire.
After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.
entries.name: Spinneret

entries: You ignore movement restrictions caused by webs, and you always know the location of any other creature in contact with the same web. While you have this knowledge, the creature cannot benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition against you.
entries.name: Web Walker

subclassFeature.name: College of the Arcane Tailor
entries: Bardic Colleges teach bards many ways to imbue their performances with arcane power. The College of Arcane Tailors dedicates itself to making costumes that enthrall and intrigue. The Bardic Regalia they create are famous for being the centerpieces of great performances and powerful arcane catalysts.

subclassFeature.name: Bardic Regalia
entries: You craft your own Bardic Regalia. The Regalia counts as magical Light Armor and provides an AC of 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use the Regalia as an Arcane Focus for your Bard spells, and you can change its appearance at will, but it always has the appearance and material of cloth.

As a Magic action, you can extend a part of your Regalia to strike your enemies. Make a melee spell attack at a target you can see within 60 feet of you. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d10} Force damage plus your Charisma modifier.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d10} when you reach Bard levels 5 ({@dice 2d10}), 11 ({@dice 3d10}), and 17 ({@dice 4d10}).

subclassFeature.name: Bewitching Raiments
entries: You always have the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell prepared. As a Magic action, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cast {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.

At Bard level 6, you also always have the {@spell Incite Greed|AI} spell prepared. As a Magic action, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cast {@spell Incite Greed|AI} without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: A Tailored Experience
entries: Your knowledge of weaving magic into the fabric of your Regalia has improved. Your Regalia can replicate a magic item from the Replicable Magic Items table below. This item does not require attunement even if it normally would.
You can only replicate one magic item at a time, and you can swap this item with another from the list after you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.caption: Replicable Magic Items
rows: Bag of Holding, Cap of Water Breathing, Cloak of Elvenkind, Cloak of the Manta Ray, Goggles of Night, Mariner's Armor, Hat of Vermin, Handy Spice Pouch, Prosthetic Limb (must look like and be made of cloth).

Bracers of Archery, Boots of the Winterlands, Cloak of Protection, Gauntlets of Ogre Power, Gloves of Missile Snaring, Gloves of Swimming and Climbing, Gloves of Thievery, Hat of Disguise, Headband of Intellect, Helm of Telepathy, Slippers of Spider Climbing, Winged Boots
Boots of Speed, Boots of Levitation, Cloak of the Bat

subclassFeature.name: It's All in the Stitching
entries: You are able to use your mastery of magical tailoring to weave spells into the fabric of your Regalia. Your  Regalia now stores spells cast into it, holding them until you choose to use them. It can store up to a number of levels worth of spells equal to your Charisma Modifier at a time.

You can cast a spell into your Regalia by touching it as the spell is cast, expending the spell slot as normal. The spell has no effect, other than to be stored in the Regalia. If the Regalia can't hold the spell, the spell is expended with no effect. These spells appear as patches on your Regalia, but are {@condition invisible} to others unless detected by the *Detect Magic* spell or similar effects.
As a Magic action, you can open one of these patches to cast any spell stored in your Regalia. The spell cast from the Regalia is no longer stored in it, freeing up space.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Dragon Song
entries: Dragons are powerful both physically and magically, their very presence inspiring many great artists. It is no wonder that bards, masters of weaving art and magic together, are drawn to these striking beings. The College of the Dragon Song is not only inspired by the imagery of dragons, but combines bardic and draconic magic to imbue its students with the same awe inspiring qualities as their school's namesake.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Fire Inspiration
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier. The next time those creatures deal damage with a weapon attack, that attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage (your choice when you activate this feature).
This damage increases by {@dice 1d6} when you reach Bard levels 5 ({@dice 2d6}), 10 ({@dice 3d6}), and 15 ({@dice 4d6}).

subclassFeature.name: Martial Training
entries: You gain proficiency in martial weapons and training with medium armor. In addition, you can use the mastery property of two kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Mantle
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you enshroud yourself in draconic might, assuming your Draconic Mantle for 1 minute. When you do so, each creature of your choice within 60 feet of you that can see you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Bard spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} for the duration of this feature.

This transformation ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or die. Once you use this feature, you can use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration (no action required).
While transformed, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Intimidating Presence
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks and you are immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Spectral Wings
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Song
entries: Your mastery of the Dragon Song is at its pinnacle, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Breath Weapon
entries: As part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to activate Draconic Mantle and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns while your Draconic Mantle is active, you can exhale a burst of elemental power in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} or 60-foot {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d10} + your Charisma modifier Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage (your choice each time you use this breath weapon) on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Wings Unfurled
entries: Magical wings are now a permanent fixture of your body. You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
